text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert: runtime-serving latency and in-flight queue growth observed for prod-us-east-1. Severity: customer-impacting. Paging oncall.

maya: I see the spike, 95th up to 4.2s and token errors starting. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/alerts/2746504321 :eyes:

aj: confirmed, requests piling in front of model-prod-v2, per-shard in_flight ~120 (threshold 64). TTL timeouts increasing.

maya: first actions: set aggressive shedding for non-critical routes + reduce max_inflight on model-prod-v2 pool. I'm going to try rate-limit rule for high-traffic tenants.

sasha: which tenants? we should avoid throttling our top-paying low-latency customers.

maya: plan: 1) apply per-tenant soft-cap: 100rpm -> 60rpm for anonymous and free-tier only; 2) reduce max_inflight from 64 -> 32 for model-prod-v2; 3) enable proxy-level shedding for long prefix chains; 4) disable heavy batching endpoint for embeddings temporarily.

leo: ack. I'll push config. running commands now.

ops-bot: Executing: `rlctl set-rate --selector tier=free,anon --rate 60rpm --scope prod-us-east-1`

ops-bot: Executing: `runtimectl update-pool --name model-prod-v2 --max-inflight 32 --region us-east-1`

carla: adding a canary for critical_tenant=acme: `rlctl set-exception --tenant acme --rate 400rpm` so we don't affect them.

maya: good call. Also flip feature flag: `ffctl set live_shedding_enabled true --env prod`

ops-bot: Feature flag updated. live_shedding_enabled=true

aj: I'm seeing CPU on host-gpu-12 spike, but queue length drops after the max_inflight change. latency 95th moved from 4.2s -> 2.1s in ~30s.

sasha: any customers reporting errors? support queue shows a few chatter from test accounts, not major customers.

maya: sent advisory to cs: "We are applying temporary traffic shaping in region us-east-1 to stabilize latencies. If you see errors, please reply here."

carla: running a quick traffic-shaper to drain long-running requests: `tcctl set-shape --pool model-prod-v2 --timeout-ms 4500` so requests over 4.5s will be aborted and retried.

ops-bot: `tcctl` applied. Active timeout 4500ms.

aj: small collateral: some internal batch jobs time out now. I've pinned those to background-queue and bumped their quota. `quotactl adjust --service batch-exports --region us-east-1 --quota 2`

maya: good. Also adding a temporary route to fallback model (model-prod-v1-quant) for low-priority requests: `routectl add --from route=/generate/lowpri --to model-prod-v1-quant --percentage 100`

ops-bot: Route added.

leo: metrics look stable-ish: 95th ~1.9s, 99th ~3.5s, error rate decreased by 60% compared to peak.

sasha: can we keep shedding on for 15 more mins then slowly relax? want to watch for oscillations.

maya: yes. I'll keep monitor and we can roll back in steps: max_inflight 32 -> 48 -> 64, rate 60rpm -> 80 -> 100 over 20m windows.

aj: noted. I'm going to update the incident runbook with actions taken. snippet:
```
- incident 2746504321 actions:
  - rlctl set-rate free-tier 60rpm
  - runtimectl update-pool model-prod-v2 max-inflight 32
  - ffctl set live_shedding_enabled true
  - tcctl set-shape model-prod-v2 timeout-ms 4500
  - routectl add fallback for lowpri -> model-prod-v1-quant
```

carla: thumbs on logs: some clients are retrying aggressively causing spikes. We should add 429 backoff header recommendations to SDKs. filing SDK PR.

maya: good follow-up. For now, leaving a note: engineering: add short-term header 'Retry-After' for 429s.

ops-bot: Observability check: trace sampling increased for this window, saved traces to incident bucket: s3://incidents/2746504321/traces.tar.gz

aj: handing off oncall to @aj (me) for the next 40m — I'll monitor metrics and control-plane commands. maya handing off to aj now.

maya: handing off, feel free to escalate to infra if we see host-level OOMs. I'm stepping off but reachable. :thumbsup: 

aj: will do. current status: mitigations applied, metrics improving, customers mostly OK. continuing to monitor and will coordinate rollback cadence.

incident-bot: Incident 2746504321 status updated: mitigations in place, oncall owner: aj.

leo: leaving a note to post root-cause follow-up once we have traces parsed — likely the new agg-batcher caused request amplification.

carla: create postmortem stub and assign owners.

aj: thanks team. feel free to ping in this thread for any new regressions. :eyes:
